title: Refuse readings that overfill a prompt set before dispatch
summary: Before dispatch, for any reading whose deliverables include a prompt file (crates/athena-context/prompts/*.md), compute token headroom (budget minus the estimate that check_budget returns, the figure the budgets test prints) for every set containing that file. Attach it to the reading and refuse the reading when the planned addition exceeds the smallest headroom. Also give the producer the scoped budgets test command. Audience: Athena operators and producers.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and integration tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria require a test showing the near-limit reading refused before dispatch.
Done is the refusal observed, not the headroom function existing.
One focused gate plus the producer command.
Enforced by a code gate and test, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Prompt files are those under crates/athena-context/prompts/ (contract, reader, producer, verifier, planner, critic) plus capability sections that feed producer and verifier sets.
The planned addition is estimated from the reading (e.g. a stated size or the request text), using the same ceil(bytes/3.0) estimator as check_budget.
The check lives in the reading-to-dispatch path in athena-core, reusing the set composition now duplicated in the budgets test.
Refusal means the reading is rejected with a message; automatically moving the edit to another file is out of scope, only suggested.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs (run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets) builds a reading that adds text to a prompt file in a set near its limit, such as contract.md, which is in every set, and shows the pre-dispatch check refuses it with an error naming the file, the planned addition, and the smallest headroom.

A companion test shows a reading with a small addition to the same file, or an edit to a file used by fewer sets with enough headroom, is accepted; readings touching no prompt files are unaffected (cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets).

A unit test shows the headroom for each prompt file equals the budget minus the check_budget estimate for every set including it, with the contract file mapped to all sets and the minimum taken (cargo test -p athena-context).

The producer's brief contains the scoped command cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets -- --nocapture, shown by a test on the rendered brief; the refusal message suggests moving the edit to a file used by fewer sets.
The reading's accepted form carries the per-set headroom figures for the target prompt files, and docs/system-facts.md still matches computed values (system_facts_budgets_match_computed passes).
cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets pass with no warnings, and cargo fmt --check is clean.

out_of_scope: Automatically rewriting the reading to move edits to another file
departures: Larger than the reference: it needs a new gate in the dispatch path, a refactor of duplicated set composition, and cross-crate tests.
hard_reason: It changes the gate that decides which readings are dispatched, so a mistake would wrongly refuse or admit jobs.
